Change c0141. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): My journey was very melancholy.

1818 text: At first I wished to hurry on, for I longed to console and sympathize with my loved and sorrowing friends; but when I drew near my native town, I slackened my progress.

1831 text: At first I wished to hurry on, for I longed to console and sympathise with my loved and sorrowing friends; but when I drew near my native town, I slackened my progress.

Diff: At first I wished to hurry on, for I longed to console and [-sympathize-] {+sympathise+} with my loved and sorrowing friends; but when I drew near my native town, I slackened my progress.

Context after (unchanged): I could hardly sustain the multitude of feelings that crowded into my mind.

result.rationale: Only orthography changes: 'sympathize' becomes 'sympathise' (British spelling); the wording, meaning, and sentence structure are unchanged.
